faq.q: Can I make beauty UGC ads from one product photo?
faq.a: Yes. Upload a clear, straight-on photo and choose a routine, swatch, unboxing, or review scene. The same source can also guide a white background photo; compare the shade and package before posting.

faq.q: Can I make before-and-after videos for a skincare product?
faq.a: No. We do not recommend before-and-after skin results because a generated face is not evidence of what your product does. Show application, texture, and packaging instead, and keep result claims out of the ad.

faq.q: Will the video match my exact foundation or lipstick shade?
faq.a: Color comes from your photo and your wording, so shoot in daylight and name the shade plainly, such as “warm beige liquid” or “brick red matte.” If the tone drifts, make another version; the credit cost is shown before each one.

faq.q: Can I add my price or a promo code to the image?
faq.a: Type prices, promo codes, and product names afterward in Canva or CapCut. AI lettering can be misspelled, so keep the generated image clean and add the words yourself.

faq.q: What kind of product photo should I upload for skincare?
faq.a: Use a straight-on shot with the label area toward the camera, on a plain surface, with no hands or clutter. Glossy tubes and clear glass pick up glare, so shoot beside a window rather than using flash.

faq.q: How long should a beauty ad video be?
faq.a: Pick 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds for feed ads. Use a shorter length for one action such as a swatch or pump, and 30 seconds for a longer routine; the credit cost is shown before each length.

faq.q: Can I run the videos as paid beauty ads?
faq.a: Yes. Downloaded clips are watermark-free and licensed for commercial use, including paid social ads. Keep result or ingredient claims accurate, and add text in your editor so it can be checked before posting.

faq.q: Is an AI creator video different from hiring a real UGC creator?
faq.a: Yes. You upload one photo and pay credits per clip instead of a creator rate, usage fees, and revision rounds. The person is AI-generated and not a real customer, so present the video as an ad rather than an independent review.
